S1.rationale: The AG2 Agent owns its model/tool-feedback operational loop and optional subtask/knowledge APIs at the frozen v1.0 review boundary. This evidence alone does not identify an S1 malfunction or bounded model/tool behavior that should be changed in a new contribution.

S2.rationale: The built-in DiscussionAdapter's expected_next_speaker turn protocol rejects out-of-turn speech and propagates channel expectation feedback to interacting Agent units. This is a real deterministic S2 attenuation of conversational collisions; no documented flaw in that witness establishes a native S2 change.

S3.rationale: Hub health, RuleBasedArbiter and resource/access limits enforce developer-provided network rules, not an owner that exercises discretionary whole-current cross-agent management. This gap does not prove framework users need a built-in S3 supervisor or that a specific manager policy is compatible.

S3*.rationale: Hub AuditLog/listeners consume the same WAL/channel state, without independent supplementary evidence or corrective governance closure. A current AG2 eval task-ID bug is a separate eval integrity issue in an evolved subsystem outside the v1.0 Index boundary and is not retroactively attributed to S3*.

S4.rationale: AG2 tools, knowledge/assembly, history and app-defined workflows can support task-time adaptation but do not provide an autonomous externally prospective organization-change loop. No native feature demand for an S4 component can be derived from this alone.

S5.rationale: Passports, Rule enforcement, auth adapters and HITL hooks establish application-supplied operational policy but not an ultimate identity conflict-to-authority-to-return relationship. This is a compositional framework rather than an implied need for a built-in S5 policymaker.
